I've been working this land for 35 years. I know what Quzhou's soil asks of me, and I know what my family needs. Let me think through each crop.

**Cotton (my backbone crop):** Cotton has fed my family for decades. I'll put 6 mu into it — the biggest share, as always. I'll use the Bt hybrid seeds from the county agricultural station. I've switched to them years ago; they cut down on bollworm spraying and the yields are steadier. I still have to watch for aphids early and spider mites in August. With my well, I can irrigate when the bolls are setting — that's when it matters most. I'll rotary till before planting like I always do. Five irrigations should cover a normal year.

**Cauliflower (2 mu):** I grow cauliflower in autumn, after my cotton fields free up some labor. I plant it on a separate 2 mu plot. I can sell it at the county market before winter. I know the fertilizer schedule by heart — this crop drinks nitrogen. Six waterings because autumn in Hebei can be dry and the heads need moisture to form tight.

**Stevia (1.5 mu):** I've had a purchasing contract with a processing company for four years now. Stevia is steady — they come pick it up, I don't have to haggle at the market. It doesn't need as much management as cotton. I'll give it the remaining 1.5 mu. It's a summer crop, goes in around the same time as cotton. Fewer pest problems than cotton, thankfully.

My water costs money — every hour the pump runs is electricity. So I don't over-irrigate. I apply fertilizer based on what I've seen work on my land, not what the bags say. I've been watching this soil since I was 23.
